annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Innocent victim of attack by South Carolina primate (9)': SC and APE come from 'South Carolina primate' but no clue word supplies GOAT; 'attack' gives nothing, so the clue looks misread or cut short.
annotationWithheld.clue: Innocent victim of attack by South Carolina primate

clue.text: What millions died-that might be great! (Camp bell: 'Pleasures of hope')

definitions.text: What millions died-that might be great! (Camp bell: 'Pleasures of hope')

parts.words: What millions died-that might be great! (Camp bell: 'Pleasures of hope')
parts.note: a quotation from Thomas Campbell's poem The Pleasures of Hope with one word left out: the name of the Roman general whose greatness cost millions their lives

explanation.walkthrough: The full line reads 'What millions died — that ___ might be great!'; the solver supplies the missing name of the Roman dictator. 'Camp bell' is the poet Campbell, split in the printing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the poet's line is the name of the Roman dictator whose conquests killed millions.

clue.text: Charge for a basic textbook

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a simple schoolbook costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the small explosive charge that sets off a larger one, and also an elementary reading book for beginners.

clue.text: Gloomier German accommodates Spanish king

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the German abbreviation holds the Spanish word inside it

parts.note: rey is the Spanish word for king

explanation.surface: A rather downcast German puts up a visiting Spanish monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey skies and moods are dull and dismal, so a more grey day is a more dismal one.

clue.text: Fish and beer given to the missus

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
the missus is informal for one's wife

explanation.surface: A husband serves fish and a pint to his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American herring-like species found in rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Cooked mint pies containing nothing but sweet peppers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of mint pies hold the round figure for nothing within them
cooking turns raw ingredients into something else, so the letters of mint pies are rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A baker's mince-pie batch somehow ends up as nothing but peppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges MINTPIES into PIMIENTS, and 'containing' puts O inside it before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimientos are the mild red capsicums used to stuff olives, a variety of sweet pepper.

clue.text: Drat! A suet pudding is full of fat

indicators.note: a pudding mixes its ingredients together, so the letters of the three words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook curses on finding a suet pudding is greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' rearranges the nine letters of DRAT A SUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturated fats are the solid animal fats such as suet, so something saturated is loaded with that kind of fat.

clue.text: SOCIALIST PARTY AHEAD IN POLL!

parts.note: the clue is printed as a newspaper headline: the main item on the front page, and also Labour leading the opinion polls

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make the clue look like a headline; read as two words it is also the left-wing party taking the lead in the poll.
explanation.definitionFit: The front-page headline item a newspaper gives most prominence to is its principal news item.

clue.text: Denunciation of one in commerce

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for one is placed inside the word for commerce

parts.note: trade is buying and selling, commerce
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A businessman is publicly attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism, a verbal attack on someone.

clue.text: Survivor in action is set free

indicators.note: the word for one who lives is placed inside the word for an act

parts.note: a deed is an action
a liver is one who lives, a survivor

explanation.surface: A soldier who came through combat is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Survivor' is LIVER in its rare sense of someone who lives on, not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue or release them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Drink adds up to 51

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Drink adds up to 51 (6)': LI is 51 (L plus I adds up to 51), but no clue word supplies QUID, so the clue looks misread or cut short.

clue.text: Madcap had the audacity to confront criminal

indicators.note: to confront is to stand face to face, so the first piece is set directly before the second

parts.note: to dare is to have the audacity, so dared
evil, wicked, as criminal acts are

explanation.surface: A reckless person bravely stood up to a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a wildly reckless person, one who takes foolish risks for thrills.

clue.text: Popular diplomacy remains unchanged

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
tact is skill in handling people, diplomacy

explanation.surface: A well-liked approach to foreign affairs stays the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left whole and undamaged has not been altered in any way.

clue.text: Black Beauty proved an unexpected winner

parts.note: dark means black in colour
Black Beauty is the horse in Anna Sewell's novel, so Beauty stands for a horse

explanation.surface: The famous fictional horse came from nowhere to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Beauty' reads as the title of Anna Sewell's novel, but the two words work separately, the second standing for the famous horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a little-known contender who surprisingly wins, from racing slang.

clue.text: He abhors Hell's open-door policy

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, Hell, so Hell's gives Dis's
an open door says to all comers: come in

explanation.surface: A man disapproves of the underworld letting everyone in.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for Hell; Dis's open-door policy is to tell all comers to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who disagrees with and objects to established beliefs is one who rejects and detests them.

clue.text: Anaemic holy man in eastern biblical land

parts.note: anaemic people look pale
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking saint lives in an eastern country of the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of the Holy Land between the Jordan and the Mediterranean is a country named in the Bible.

clue.text: You receive a vote in the affirmative

indicators.note: the old word for you takes in the next letter, which follows it

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: You are given a ballot to say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes, used as a spoken vote in favour in a legislature.

clue.text: Longing to obtain foreign currency

explanation.surface: A traveller yearns to get some overseas money.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a craving or desire, and also the monetary unit of Japan.

clue.text: BR's future high-speed train initially proved suitable

explanation.surface: British Rail's planned fast train turned out fit for purpose at first.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail; its Advanced Passenger Train of the 1980s was known by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilting train of the period went by its initials, and the same three letters mean fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Inspire a friend from Ulster

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster
mate means friend

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish pal provides encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate someone is to give them life and spirit, to fill them with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Individual in the dock who breaks new ground

indicators.note: the word for a single person is placed inside the landing-stage word

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage or dock for ships
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A defendant standing trial turns out to be a trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dock' suggests a criminal trial, but the dock is the harbour sort, a PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one who first explores or settles new territory, or leads in a new field.

clue.text: Teaching union could be a hard one to crack

explanation.surface: A teachers' union proves a tough negotiating opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The NUT was the National Union of Teachers, and a nut is a hard-shelled fruit, proverbially difficult to crack.

clue.text: Honest expression of support for justice

parts.note: up, as in a fan's cry 'Up the Rovers!', expresses support
right means justice, what is fair

explanation.surface: A frank declaration backing the cause of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is morally straight, trustworthy and honourable.

clue.text: Sergeant-Major English gets in supplies-but that's the lot

indicators.note: the military abbreviation and the letter for English go inside the word for equipment

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment or supplies

explanation.surface: An English NCO collects provisions and declares that is everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lot' reads as 'everything', but here it means one's lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, one's allotted portion in life.

clue.text: Up-to date operating system by the British navy

parts.note: a mode is a way or system of operating
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A computer is brought current with the help of the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modern is current, belonging to the present day.

clue.text: Clearly the economy was a resounding success!

definitions.text: Clearly the economy was a resounding success!

parts.words: Clearly the economy was a resounding success!
parts.note: a thriving economy is said to flourish rapidly, and a resounding sound is a deep echoing roar; one verb covers both

explanation.walkthrough: 'resounding' hides its literal sense: the word fits both a loud reverberating noise and a sharp rise in trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes both a deep echoing roar and a period of rapid economic growth.

clue.text: Riddling instruction to the procrastinating victor

definitions.text: Riddling instruction to the procrastinating victor

parts.words: Riddling instruction to the procrastinating victor
parts.note: to riddle is to sieve, so the word means separate grain from chaff, while split in two it tells a dawdling champion to take the prize at once

explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is a coarse sieve; read as two words, the answer is a command to win without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnowing blows the chaff away from grain, a sifting like the work of a riddle or sieve.

clue.text: Therefore, put no male in charge of work study

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: So a manager decides no man should run the efficiency review.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics is the study of people's efficiency in their working environment.

clue.text: One art-form which is highly embellished

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the six letters are moulded into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A style of art that is lavishly decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art-form' hides the anagram signal: 'form' rearranges ONE and ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, with much ornament.

clue.text: Privates take part in a salute by general consent

indicators.note: the ordinary soldiers go into the middle of the welcome

parts.note: to greet is to salute
men are the rank and file, privates as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers join in saluting a general, by common accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like the officer being saluted, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When opinions match and everybody is of one mind, there is accord or concord.

clue.text: The Princess Royal is retiring to the shade

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the princess's name and the next word run backwards

parts.note: Princess Anne holds the title of the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: Princess Anne goes off to sit in the cool out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the princess's name and 'is' round together. 'shade' suggests shelter from sunlight, but here it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brownish-yellow pigment, so a colour or tint.

clue.text: Stall-holder is obviously preparing to go off duty

definitions.text: Stall-holder is obviously preparing to go off duty

parts.words: Stall-holder is obviously preparing to go off duty
parts.note: a market trader packing up dismantles a stall; the phrase for that literal action also means to leave a post

explanation.walkthrough: A trader packing up literally takes the stand down, the same phrase as for leaving one's post.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to withdraw from a post or come off duty, as troops do.
